proposed.demonstrated_gap: The installed gh-address-comments (openai/skills@49f948fa, a stale source) runs fetch_comments.py, asks the user which numbered comments to address and applies fixes (SKILL.md lines 15-22). It has no step that replies to or resolves a review thread, and the main ruleset requires thread resolution. ce-resolve-pr-feedback judges inline threads, review bodies and top-level comments centrally and publishes fixes before replying. It resolves threads with the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation (scripts/resolve-pr-thread), re-fetches to confirm resolution (references/full-mode.md line 266) and keeps needs-human threads open. It never pauses to ask (SKILL.md line 14), which fits the AGENTS.md rule against approval steps for bounded work, and it excludes merge, rebase, force-push and CI approval (line 18). Without subagents it applies the fixes itself, one at a time (full-mode.md line 116). Maintained: 32 commits on the skill path, 7 since 2026-09-07, latest 2026-10-01 (#1820); the repository passes the 90-day rule. It reaches Codex through .codex-plugin/plugin.json (skills ./skills/) and has no agents/openai.yaml. Two install constraints. First, for judgment-bound items its rubric asks the sibling ce-pov for an 'oracle' cross-model panel (references/evaluation-rubric.md lines 81-88). ce-pov then sends the subject to other installed model CLIs (ce-pov references/cross-model-panel.md lines 18-20, 95-98 and 530), which would start a cross-family lane from inside a skill. Installing this folder alone leaves ce-pov unavailable, and the rubric then returns needs-human (line 88). Second, its allowed-tools (Bash(bash *), Bash(python3 *)) pre-approve any bash or python3 command in Claude Code while it is active. Cost risk for the layer's rule: SKILL.md is 6,684 bytes plus on-demand references (full-mode.md 32,043 bytes, evaluation-rubric.md 19,090 bytes), against 1,278 bytes for gh-address-comments.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: It covers all three streams of this task in one local loop, which no installed skill does. Review comments go to ce-resolve-pr-feedback. CI failures go to ce-debug, and flaky or infrastructure failures are rerun with gh run rerun --failed. Branch-currency items come from a deterministic snapshot (SKILL.md lines 9 and 47-50). The critic's two questions check out. It runs locally: 'The loop runs gh, git, and a bundled Python helper against a local checkout with filesystem access' (references/setup.md line 5). The helper scripts/pr-snapshot is stdlib-only Python (179,950 bytes) that wakes the agent only when there is work. It fits Codex: references/watch-loop.md line 22 gives the Codex CLI recipe (exec_command, then write_stdin), beside Claude Code's background Bash with Monitor, or ScheduleWakeup under /loop (line 19); both are session-bound. For conflicts, a BEHIND branch is updated with the host's update-branch call and expected_head_sha. A DIRTY branch gets an exact-base local merge that resolves only a previewed mechanical conflict and never rebases or force-pushes (references/branch-currency.md lines 16-17). That matches the merge path in docs/lanes.md lines 129-135, but not the evidence.json re-registration steps (lines 100-111). Kept for later comparison for four reasons. It needs at least four sibling skills from one pin: ce-resolve-pr-feedback, ce-debug, ce-commit-push-pr, and ce-noslop through the PR-description writer (ce-commit-push-pr references/pr-description-writing.md line 14). It must be installed without ce-pov, whose 'oracle' panel would start a cross-family lane. It refreshes a drifted PR description before reporting ready (SKILL.md line 55); that writer treats repository PR templates as a minimum structural contract (pr-description-writing.md line 18), so the required '## SOTA sources' heading should survive, but whether a rewrite keeps the section's content is untested. Its value also depends on ce-resolve-pr-feedback passing first. It authorizes fix, commit, push, reply and resolve without asking (line 29). Two points were not verified: whether ce-commit-push-pr in mode:pipeline skips its interactive preview-and-confirm step, and whether ce-debug asks questions in pipeline mode. Maintained: 44 commits on the skill path, all within the last 90 days, 5 since 2026-09-07, latest 2026-09-21 (#1754).

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Complement to variant-analysis, replacing nothing. The layer's recorded gap is siblings of an already fixed defect that were found only after merge: #314 widened #291's blob exclusion and closed sentences the #269 filter missed. variant-analysis searches for candidates statically. No installed skill checks before merge that a fix covers its root cause's variants. post-patch-validation does. Its evidence contract requires a `variant` check that must fail on the vulnerable base and pass on the patch (SKILL.md:93). The check runs side-blind in isolated worktrees and must print a PPV_REACHED marker. Findings and validation gaps are reported separately. Upstream's frozen `missed-variant` eval is exactly this case: a patch that fixes the demonstrated instance and misses repeats. The manifest's exclusion reason ('duplicates fp-check') does not hold on merit. fp-check returns a TRUE/FALSE POSITIVE verdict on one suspected bug, and its SKILL.md never mentions patches, baselines or variants. The runner is stdlib-only (PEP 723 `dependencies = []`), so `uv run` installs no code. Conditions that still apply: (1) The manifest's audit condition is unmet: Socket Warn, audited 2026-09-15, for offensive testing plus Bash/Workflow execution. A trial winner still needs that resolved or an explicit re-decision before adoption. (2) Every plan must also include `exploit` and `security` checks, so the skill is shaped for security patches. #269's blind-packet leak fits. A pure logic bug needs its original assertion recast as the exploit check. (3) It executes repository code with the caller's privileges and is not a sandbox, so the trial runs in an isolated root. proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run a skill-creator paired benchmark with arms with_skill and without_skill (installed skills only), 3 runs per case, in Claude Code and in Codex, inside an isolated root. Frozen fixed-defect set: (1) the upstream post-patch-validation evals at 82fe8226 (missed-variant, complete-fix, behavior-regression, mixed-failures); (2) the variant-analysis tests/ground-truth.json gradio fixture, with the seed patched and the cross-module variant and decoy left in; (3) this repo's #291 and #269 fixes, replayed at their pre-#314 commits, with #314's siblings as the known answers. Arms: with_skill = variant-analysis plus post-patch-validation; without_skill = installed variant-analysis alone. Metrics: assertion pass rate for 'known missed sibling reported as a supported finding' (recall); assertion pass rate for 'no missed-variant finding and decoy not reported on complete fixes' (precision); total_tokens and duration_ms from timing.json. Decision rule: it wins the trial only if with_skill's mean pass rate beats without_skill by more than one standard deviation with no added false findings. Executed checks will cost more, so the layer's no-higher-cost rule fails unless the token and time delta is justified by siblings that would otherwise reach main. The Socket Warn condition must also be cleared before adoption.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Official Anthropic alternative to the bundled /security-review for checking changes before merge. 'Scan changes' covers a branch diff, a PR diff or one commit (README:36). A finding reaches the report only after independent verifiers, told to disprove it, confirm it. Its confidence is capped by a verification record computed in code (README:70-72). It is not targeted, for these reasons. It is plugin-bound (Agent(claude-security:*), Workflow(claude-security:scan), ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} scripts), so it cannot run in Codex and cannot meet this layer's both-clients overturn rule. It has no fixed-defect variant search and publishes no precision or recall. The layer's overturn metric (more true issues, fewer false ones) is exactly what promptfoo's maintained skill-comparison examples score.
